# MUI Yew Example

This example demonstrates how to compose the shared `mui-shared` primitives
(routes, layout, automation identifiers, and theme metadata) with the
[Yew](https://yew.rs) framework. The application mirrors the archival Material
UI Next.js demo by:

* bootstrapping a router from the shared typed descriptors so navigation is
  deterministic across SSR and CSR renders,
* rendering the shared layout skeleton (headline, body copy, CTAs, and the
  ProTip footer) with `rustic_ui_system` primitives, and
* attaching `data-rustic-*` automation hooks generated by `mui-shared` so QA and
  observability tooling can probe the DOM without brittle selectors.

## Development (CSR)

```bash
trunk serve --open
```

The client bundle hydrates the SSR markup by default. Every navigation element
and layout node exposes deterministic automation identifiers (for example
`data-rustic-app-navigation="app-home-navigation"`).

## Routing orchestration

`yew_router` is wired to the shared `HOME`/`ABOUT` descriptors. The router feeds
those descriptors into `mui_shared::layout::AppShell` so the SSR and CSR code
paths render identical markup. The example intentionally renders navigation
links and calls-to-action using the same metadata to keep localisation and
accessibility reviews centralised in the shared crate.

## Mode switch state machine

The theme switcher is implemented as a documented state machine. During SSR the
component renders inert markup in the `HydrationPhase::Server` state so the
output is deterministic. Once hydrated the effect transitions to
`HydrationPhase::Client`, captures the system colour preference via
`matchMedia`, and dispatches events so automation can observe
`ModeAction::Select` transitions. The machine preserves the recorded system
preference when toggling back to the "System" option, mirroring the original
React behaviour.

## Server-side rendering

```bash
cargo run --manifest-path examples/mui-yew/Cargo.toml --features ssr > prerendered.html
# serve `prerendered.html` and hydrate it with the client bundle
trunk build --release
```

The SSR entry point composes `mui_shared::layout::AppShell::render_ssr_document`
with `yew::ServerRenderer` so the generated HTML already contains deterministic
`data-rustic-*` identifiers. Hydration attaches to the shared
`data-rustic-app-hydration-root` marker emitted for the Yew framework.

## Testing

```bash
cargo test --package rustic_ui_yew_example
```

The unit tests validate the router-to-descriptor mapping, automation identifier
determinism, and the mode switch state transitions. These guardrails ensure
future refactors continue to hydrate cleanly while keeping automation hooks
stable for synthetic monitoring.
